glossary.line: Baiting: you poke and wait for a reaction because you have nothing else. Everyone sees the hook. Nobody's biting.
Deflection: 'just a joke', 'you're too sensitive'. You moved the target because you can't defend the shot. Weak dodge.
Dehumanizing: calling people animals or filth so harm feels okay. It says nothing about them and everything about you.
Pile-on: needing a crowd to win one argument. If your point was strong, you wouldn't need backup. Numbers aren't proof.
Slur swap: a stand-in word with the same meaning. Changing the spelling doesn't change the message. We all read it.
Slur evasion: dots, spaces, l33t to sneak it past a filter. The filter missed it. People didn't. Still a slur.
Code words: hate dressed up as inside jokes. Thinking nobody gets it is the funny part. People get it.
Slur: a word built to demean people for who they are. Not edgy, not brave, just lazy. Not here.
Gaslighting: insisting what everyone saw didn't happen. The chat log exists. Rewriting history only works on people who weren't there.
Whataboutism: can't defend your point, so you point at someone else. Everyone sees the dodge. Answer the question or admit you can't.
Concern trolling: fake worry to tear someone down. If you cared, you'd sound different. The mask is see-through.
Strawman: you argue with a fake version of what they said because the real one beat you. Fight the real point or sit down.
Goalpost moving: they met your demand, so you made a new one. That's not debate, that's running away slowly.
Sealioning: endless 'polite' questions you don't want answered, just to wear people out. Fake curiosity is still harassment.
Tone policing: attacking how something was said because you can't touch what was said. The point still stands.
Ad hominem: attacking the person because the argument beat you. Insults are what's left when the logic runs out.
Gish gallop: twenty weak claims fired at once, hoping nobody checks. Quantity isn't quality. Pick your best one. Oh wait.
Just asking questions: smuggling a claim in as a 'question' so you can't be held to it. Say what you mean or own that you won't.
Victim blaming: making the hurt person the problem so the one who hurt them walks free. Obvious, and ugly.
Othering: painting a group as 'not like us' so mistreating them feels fine. Old trick, same tired result.
Scapegoating: blaming one group for everything because real answers are hard. Easy target, lazy thinking.
Stereotyping: judging millions of people by one cartoon. Says more about your imagination than about them.
Dog piling: jumping on someone already outnumbered. Joining late to kick isn't bravery. It's following.
Trolling: saying things you don't believe to get a rise. If the reaction is your whole goal, you've got nothing. We see it.
Flaming: all heat, no point. Shouting louder doesn't make you more right, just easier to ignore.
Doxxing threats: hinting you'll expose someone's private info to scare them. It's intimidation, it breaks the rules, and it's logged.
Outing: exposing someone's private identity to hurt them. Not truth-telling. Just cruelty with an excuse.
Misgendering on purpose: refusing someone's name for themselves to get a rise. Cheap, petty, and everyone notices.
Deadnaming: using an old name on purpose to wound. Remembering it isn't the flex you think it is.
Mocking accents: when you can't beat what someone says, you mock how they say it. Tells us you lost the point.
Love bombing: drowning someone in flattery to hook them fast. Too much, too soon is a tactic, not a feeling.
Negging: backhanded 'compliments' to knock someone down so they chase approval. Transparent and tired.
Guilt tripping: making someone feel bad so they do what you want. If you need guilt to win, you didn't have a reason.
Silent treatment: freezing someone out to punish them. Ignoring isn't strength, it's control with the volume off.
Rumor spreading: hurting someone where they can't answer back. If it were true, you'd say it to their face.
Impersonation: pretending to be someone to make them look bad. You had to borrow a name because yours has no weight.
Spam flooding: burying the chat so nobody else can talk. Volume isn't a voice. It's just noise.
Brigading: calling in outsiders to swarm one room. Needing an army for one chat says it all.
False equivalence: treating a paper cut and a broken leg as 'the same'. They aren't. Everyone can tell.
Appeal to tradition: 'it's always been this way'. So was a lot of bad stuff. Old isn't the same as right.
Minimizing: 'it's not a big deal' about harm you caused. You don't get to decide how much it hurt someone else.
DARVO: deny, attack, then play the victim. Flipping the script so fast is the tell. We saw the order it happened in.
Triangulation: pulling a third person in to gang up or stir jealousy. Can't handle it one on one? Noted.
Intimidation: trying to scare people quiet because you can't win the argument. Fear isn't a point. It's a confession.
Threats: the last move of someone who's lost. Against Xat rules, logged, and it changes nothing here.
Sarcasm attack: mocking instead of answering so you never have to commit to a point. Smirking isn't an argument.
Emoji harassment: spamming clown or vomit emojis at someone. Tiny pictures, tiny argument. Still harassment.
Projection: accusing others of exactly what you're doing. Funny how specific those accusations get.
Changing the subject: losing on one topic, so you jump to another. Come back when you can finish the first one.
Floyding: turning a man's death into a meme to bait a reaction. Not edgy, just a cheap shock tactic from someone with nothing to say. Nobody's taking the bait.
Fake neutrality: 'both sides are bad' to shield the side doing harm. Sitting on the fence still picks a side.
